detailed_rationale: Transrail Lighting is a power transmission-and-distribution (T&D) EPC contractor, with T&D representing 90-92% of revenue and a diversified order book spanning India, Africa and other export geographies. Growth has been consistent rather than lumpy: 3-year revenue CAGR of ~30% and 1-year growth of ~30% are closely matched (no material acceleration or deceleration divergence), and the order book stood at Rs 14,733 crore as of December 2025 - roughly 2x current annualized revenue, giving genuine multi-year visibility. ROCE of ~29% is healthy for an EPC business (which is inherently working-capital intensive), and D/E of ~0.30 is manageable. The company recently declared a Rs 3/share dividend and approved a Rs 600 crore QIP for FY27, which will fund working capital and growth capex for the expanding order book but represents a modest, board-approved dilution rather than a distress-driven capital raise. Q1 FY27 results were not yet released as of this review (expected in the July-August window); this assessment is anchored on the December 2025 order-book disclosure and the trailing 3-year/1-year growth consistency, which is itself a positive signal in a sector (capital goods/EPC) known for lumpy, hard-to-predict quarterly execution.
recommendation_rationale: Quant lands on Hold; the fresh research supports continuing to hold this view rather than upgrading conviction further, though the combination of a large, well-covered order book, consistent (not decelerating) growth, and a reasonable ~17x trailing valuation is one of the more attractively balanced profiles in this batch of capital-goods names.
summary: Transrail Lighting has a large, well-diversified order book (about twice its annual revenue) supporting consistent growth in its power transmission-and-distribution EPC business, at a valuation that does not look stretched relative to that growth. A planned Rs 600 crore capital raise will fund growth but is a modest, board-approved dilution rather than a sign of financial stress.
positive_para: An order book of Rs 14,733 crore (roughly 2x annualized revenue) provides genuine multi-year revenue visibility, growth has been consistent (not decelerating) across the 3-year and 1-year windows, ROCE (~29%) is healthy for an EPC business, and the ~17x trailing valuation does not appear to be pricing in excessive optimism relative to the growth and order-book cover.
negative_para: EPC/T&D execution is inherently working-capital intensive and subject to project-timing lumpiness that can cause any single quarter to disappoint even with a strong order book; the planned Rs 600 crore QIP, while sensible for funding growth, will modestly dilute existing shareholders; and export/African-geography exposure carries incremental country and currency risk relative to a purely domestic order book.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At roughly 17x trailing earnings against ~29-30% historical and order-book-supported growth, the multiple looks reasonable rather than rich - this is one of the more attractively priced growth profiles in the current batch, provided execution against the large order book continues without major working-capital strain.
